answer: When an agent joins the PoA economy it must lock an onyx‑sized deposit, recorded in a velvet‑hashed ledger, and submit a proof‑of‑work that burns a small ember of computational effort; the deposit is automatically forfeited if the node’s identifier ever appears in a conflicting quorum. Each new identity therefore costs the attacker the full deposit plus the required proof‑of‑work time, typically 0.5 PoA tokens and 10 seconds of CPU work per head.
